parameters.query:
-- What the decline is about, and whether it is still a live question. Always one row.
WITH p AS (SELECT $1::text AS ref, $2::text AS stylist_id)
SELECT json_build_object(
  'found',       EXISTS (SELECT 1 FROM appointment a, p WHERE a.ref = p.ref),
  'status',      (SELECT a.status FROM appointment a, p WHERE a.ref = p.ref),
  'in_future',   COALESCE((SELECT a.starts_at FROM appointment a, p WHERE a.ref = p.ref) > now(), false),
  'still_theirs',COALESCE((SELECT a.stylist_id FROM appointment a, p WHERE a.ref = p.ref)
                          = (SELECT stylist_id FROM p), false),
  -- A stylist tapping decline twice must not send the customer two consent requests.
  'already_asked', EXISTS (
      SELECT 1 FROM appointment a, bot_user_profile b, client c
      WHERE a.ref = (SELECT ref FROM p) AND c.id = a.client_id
        AND b.user_key = c.channel || ':' || c.channel_user_id
        AND b.pending_booking ->> 'kind' = 'reassign'
        AND b.pending_set_at > now() - interval '30 minutes'),
  -- `p` is a scalar subquery here, not a comma-join: mixing a comma-join with JOIN puts the
  -- comma-joined table out of scope inside the ON clauses and Postgres rejects the whole query.
  'appointment', (SELECT json_build_object(
      'id', a.id, 'ref', a.ref, 'service_id', a.service_id, 'service_name', sv.name,
      'stylist_id', a.stylist_id, 'stylist_name', st.name,
      'client_id', a.client_id, 'client_name', c.name,
      'user_key', c.channel || ':' || c.channel_user_id,
      'starts_at_utc', to_char(a.starts_at AT TIME ZONE 'UTC','YYYY-MM-DD"T"HH24:MI:SS"Z"'),
      'ends_at_utc',   to_char(a.ends_at   AT TIME ZONE 'UTC','YYYY-MM-DD"T"HH24:MI:SS"Z"'),
      'starts_at_local', to_char(a.starts_at AT TIME ZONE 'Asia/Manila','Dy DD Mon, HH24:MI'))
    FROM appointment a
    JOIN service sv ON sv.id = a.service_id
    JOIN stylist st ON st.id = a.stylist_id
    JOIN client  c  ON c.id  = a.client_id
    WHERE a.ref = (SELECT ref FROM p))
) AS result;

-- Write the consent question as a server-side pending row — the same mechanism a booking
-- read-back uses. The customer's "yes" later confirms THIS, not whatever a model extracted.
-- A live conversation is never talked over.
WITH p AS (SELECT $1::text AS user_key, $2::jsonb AS pending)
UPDATE bot_user_profile b
   SET pending_booking = p.pending, pending_set_at = now(), updated_at = now()
  FROM p
 WHERE b.user_key = p.user_key AND p.pending IS NOT NULL
   AND (b.pending_booking IS NULL OR b.pending_set_at < now() - interval '30 minutes')
RETURNING b.user_key;

parameters.content:
## 32 · a stylist cannot make it

**In** `{booking_ref, stylist_id}` — the stylist who is declining.

It finds who else is free and then **asks the customer**, naming the replacement and saying plainly that they are held to the same standard. It never reassigns silently: the customer decides who touches their hair.

The question is written as a pending row on the customer's profile — the same mechanism a booking read-back uses — so their "yes" is confirmed against what they were actually shown. Tool `24` then re-checks everything at the moment of the move; if the replacement got busy in the meantime, nothing changes and the customer is told.

Nobody free? The customer is offered a reschedule or a cancellation, and a human is told. No name is invented to fill the gap.
